key.description: Where hooks can be configured and the precedence model when multiple scopes define hooks for the same event. Common scopes: global/user, project, workspace, managed/enterprise.

hook_scopes.mechanism: three-tier config scopes documented under 'System-Level' / 'User-Level' / 'Workspace-Level' headings

key.description: Whether hooks communicate with the host via structured JSON on stdin/stdout rather than plain text or exit codes alone.

json_io_protocol.mechanism: JSON event context delivered via stdin documented under 'Common Input Structure' heading

key.description: Whether the provider supports organization-level MCP configuration management, including managed server lists, allowlists, and enterprise registries.

enterprise_management.mechanism: organization-level MCP admin controls (whitelist, custom registries, regex matching) documented under 'Admin Controls (Teams & Enterprises)' / 'Admin Configuration Guidelines' headings

key.description: Whether MCP server configuration supports environment variable expansion. Reduces the need for hardcoded secrets in config files.

env_var_expansion.mechanism: ${env:VAR_NAME} and ${file:/path} interpolation documented under 'Config Interpolation' heading

key.description: Whether the provider offers an in-IDE MCP server discovery and installation experience.

marketplace.mechanism: in-IDE MCP marketplace documented under 'MCP Registry' / 'Configuring Custom Registries' headings

key.description: Which per-server tool filtering mechanisms the provider supports. Contents: {allowlist: bool, blocklist: bool, disable_flag: bool}. Controls which server tools are exposed to the agent. Boundary: tool_filtering governs tool visibility (what appears in the agent's available tool set); see auto_approve for execution gating of visible tools.

tool_filtering.mechanism: per-server tool filtering documented under 'Configuring MCP tools' (UI tool toggles, 100-tool cap) and 'MCP Whitelist' (admin-side regex matching) headings

key.description: Which MCP transport protocols the provider supports. Common transports: stdio (local process), SSE (Server-Sent Events), HTTP/streamable-HTTP (stateless or streaming).

transport_types.mechanism: transport types (stdio for local, Streamable HTTP and SSE for remote) documented under 'Remote HTTP MCPs' heading; remote servers use serverUrl/url instead of command/args

always.mechanism: always_on trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — full rule content included in system prompt every message

glob.mechanism: glob trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — activated when files matching glob pattern are in context

manual.mechanism: manual trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — activated via @-mention

model_decision.mechanism: model_decision trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — Cascade decides based on context

key.description: How rules decide when to load into context. Providers implement varying modes: always-on, conditional/glob-based, model-decision, and manual activation. Tracks which modes the provider supports and how they are configured.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-RULE §9.1 (DERIVABLE); activation-mode vocabulary ACIF-RULE Appendix A, §10

key.description: Whether the provider auto-generates persistent rules from conversation context. Distinct from user-authored rules — these are AI-created and stored separately.

auto_memory.mechanism: Cascade-managed Memories layer auto-writes context based on conversation (documented under 'Memories & Rules' / 'How to Manage Memories')

agents_md.mechanism: AGENTS.md fallback documented in dedicated rules.1 doc with 'Comparison with Rules' section

key.description: Which rule file formats from other providers this provider recognizes. Contents: recognized_formats (list of filenames like AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules). Minimum qualification: supported when the provider reads at least one rule-file format defined by a different provider.
Whether rules load from multiple directory levels with defined precedence. Enables project-root rules plus subdirectory-scoped overrides.

hierarchical_loading.mechanism: .windsurf/rules scanned in current workspace, sub-directories, and parent dirs up to git root (documented under 'Rules Discovery' / 'Rules Storage Locations')
